title: Double after every loss
hook: Lose, double the bet, repeat: the first win covers everything. Is it free money?

knows: a fair coin lands heads half the time
an average is total divided by count
doesNotKnow: why a staking rule cannot change the average of a fair game
how rare big losses balance many small wins

misconception: Doubling your bet after every loss guarantees a profit, so it beats a fair game.
objective: The learner can explain that the doubling system wins $1 with chance 63/64 and loses $63 with chance 1/64, so its average profit per round is exactly $0.
keyState: A bust seen: the profit line climbs in $1 steps, then drops $63 at once (seed 777: 32 wins, then a bust at round 33, total -$31).

claims.text: With a $1 start and doubling after each loss, six losses in a row lose $1 + $2 + $4 + $8 + $16 + $32 = $63; any earlier win ends the round $1 up.
claims.source: Sum of 2^0..2^5 = 2^6 - 1 = 63; a win at bet 2^k recovers 2^k - 1 and gains $1 (BUST in src/demos/probability/double-after-every-loss/model.ts).

claims.text: On a fair coin a round wins $1 with chance 63/64 and loses $63 with chance 1/64, so the average profit per round is exactly $0.
claims.source: P(6 losses) = (1/2)^6 = 1/64; 63/64 x 1 - 1/64 x 63 = 0 (expected() in model.ts). Option '+$0.98' is 63/64 rounded.

claims.text: The stage's rounds are one seeded run: 32 wins of $1, then a bust at round 33 (total -$31); playing on to the next bust gives round 120 (total -$8).
claims.source: rounds() in model.ts, mulberry32 seed 777, untuned (the first seed tried). The QA path (1 + 10 rounds, then until a bust) reaches round 33. Over seeds 1-1000 the first bust after round 11 came at round 13-251 (middle 95%, median 57): a run's total after one bust can be well up or down; it is not evidence about the average.

claims.text: Doubling turns many small wins into rare big losses; it cannot move the average of a fair game.
claims.source: Optional stopping / martingale property: any bounded staking rule on a fair game has expected profit 0 (c2 is the concrete case). Any textbook on martingales, e.g. Grimmett and Stirzaker, Probability and Random Processes, ch. 12.

recall.question: A friend's system on a fair game has won $1 in each of their last 40 sessions. What does that tell you about its average profit?
options: It is positive, the system works
Nothing: rare big losses can cancel the small wins exactly
recall.why: Doubling-style systems win small amounts often and lose big amounts rarely. On a fair game the two balance to an average of $0, however long the winning streak looks.
